questions.prompt: The Great Fire of London occurred in which year?
questions.fact: It destroyed most of the medieval city but the recorded death toll was remarkably low, probably because it spread slowly enough to flee.

questions.prompt: What is the term for animals that maintain a constant body temperature?
questions.fact: Maintaining it is metabolically expensive, which is why such animals must eat far more than cold-blooded ones of similar size.

questions.prompt: Which country won the first FIFA World Cup in 1930?
questions.fact: It hosted the tournament too, and only four European teams made the long sea crossing to take part.

questions.prompt: Which band released the album 'Abbey Road'?
questions.fact: It was the last album they recorded together, though not the last released.

questions.prompt: What is the capital of Cuba?
questions.fact: Its old town is a UNESCO site, and the harbour was fortified heavily because it was the assembly point for Spanish treasure fleets.

questions.prompt: Which Shakespeare play includes the line 'To be, or not to be'?
questions.fact: It is his longest play, and an uncut performance runs to roughly four hours.

questions.prompt: Which programming concept means a function calling itself?
questions.fact: Each call consumes stack space, so a version without a proper stopping condition crashes rather than looping forever.
